precepts.text: And I will bring you into the wilderness of the people, and there will I plead with you face to face. So when he pleads with us face to face, that means all thy children shall be taught of the Lord.
precepts.point: And all thy children shall be taught of the Lord; and great shall be the peace of thy children.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
Isaiah says, “And all thy children shall be taught of the Lord; and great shall be the peace of thy children.” Ezekiel shows how that teaching will happen: “And I will bring you into the wilderness of the people, and there will I plead with you face to face.”

When the Lord pleads with us face to face, that is when all the children of Israel shall be taught of the Lord. He brings the twelve tribes out and teaches them himself.

And the peace that follows is the rest of Isaiah’s promise: “In righteousness shalt thou be established: thou shalt be far from oppression; for thou shalt not fear: and from terror; for it shall not come near thee.” The twelve tribes shall be established, far from oppression, and terror shall no more come near us. Today our people are still terrorized, hanged from trees and called suicides, but the day of being taught face to face by the Lord is the day that ends.

precepts.text: A brother brought the proof of what the pleading is: for behold, the Lord will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire. For by fire and by his sword will the Lord plead with all flesh.
precepts.point: And I will cause you to pass under the rod, and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant: and I will purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me. Even after; even after the deliverance, there is still going to be a purge. There will still be bad actors among us that need to be purged, people that still need to get right, and Christ is the one who is going to give it to them. They shall not enter into the land of Israel: and ye shall know that I am the Lord.
precepts.why:
Ezekiel says, “And I will bring you into the wilderness of the people, and there will I plead with you face to face. Like as I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so will I plead with you”. This is our deliverance from Babylon: we go back into the wilderness, Christ deals with us and teaches us the laws again, and what he is doing to us there is purging.

So what kind of pleading is he going to be doing? Is it baby, baby, please? No. The pleading is killing and smiting, and Isaiah proves it: “For, behold, the Lord will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire. For by fire and by his sword will the Lord plead with all flesh”. It's not a damn R&B song.

That is the same fury Ezekiel speaks of: “surely with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out, will I rule over you”. As he pleaded with our fathers in the wilderness of Egypt, where the rebellious fell, he will plead with us, by fire and by the sword.

So even after the deliverance there is still going to be a purge. There will still be bad actors among us, people that still need to get right, and they are going to get it; Christ is the one who will give it to them.

precepts.text: I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel. No begging for them either.
precepts.point: And I will cause you to pass under the rod, and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant: and I will purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me. Even after; even after the deliverance, there is still going to be a purge. There will still be bad actors among us that need to be purged, people that still need to get right, and Christ is the one who is going to give it to them. They shall not enter into the land of Israel: and ye shall know that I am the Lord.
precepts.why:
The Lord pleads with the nations the same way he pleads with Israel. Joel says: “I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel”. No baby, baby, please for them either. He will kill them, for his people Israel.

The nations are judged “for my people and for my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land.” The pleading in the valley of Jehoshaphat is the Lord's vengeance on the ones who scattered us.

So when Ezekiel says the Lord will plead with Israel face to face in the wilderness “Like as I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt”, the word means the same thing it means for the nations: judgment, smiting and fire, not begging. He pleads for Israel against the nations, and he pleads with the rebels in Israel in the wilderness, and nobody should read either as the Lord asking nicely.

precepts.text: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.
precepts.point: And I will cause you to pass under the rod, and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant: and I will purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me. Even after; even after the deliverance, there is still going to be a purge. There will still be bad actors among us that need to be purged, people that still need to get right, and Christ is the one who is going to give it to them. They shall not enter into the land of Israel: and ye shall know that I am the Lord.
precepts.why:
Ezekiel says, “And I will purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me”. What kind of purge is he going to be doing? Killing. Matthew shows it: “Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.” Does anybody not understand that?

The wheat is gathered into the garner, and the chaff is burned. That is the rebels who “shall not enter into the land of Israel”. Zechariah is still talking about the purge: “in all the land, saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein.” And even the third that is left still has to be sifted, refined, made right, purged.

The Lord is not going to give the kingdom to wicked negroes. The kingdom will not be open to wicked negroes. To get the kingdom you have to go through this fire and get right; there is no other way. You can't keep doing what you do and think you are going to get the kingdom. It is impossible.

That is why we have to fight for this and help each other. If I see you weak and say nothing to you, that means I hate you. So if I tell you, bro, you have to fix that, and you say I hate you, shut your ass up; I am trying to save your life. We are so used to not taking correction from each other that it feels like hate, because everybody has coddled you, and you keep kicking the can down the street until you are back on the corner doing what you do. The fan is already in his hand.

precepts.text: The bond of the covenant is the new covenant. I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts. We are going to know God's laws and we will keep them. You are not going to forget the feast day and eat the donut out of routine; his laws will be in our minds, and we will do them and serve him. We are in the beginning of the new covenant now, but once Christ returns it will be fully established in the wilderness. And they shall not teach every man his neighbour, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest, because the Lord is going to teach us.
precepts.point: I will purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me: those that break God's laws, those that got leaven in them. I will bring them forth out of the country where they sojourn, and they shall not enter into the land of Israel. You will be delivered up out of that destruction, but the same way everybody was delivered up from Egypt and everybody did not make it into the promised land, there will be groups of people that will be delivered that will not make it into the promised land.
precepts.why:
Ezekiel says, “I will cause you to pass under the rod, and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant”. The rod is correction. And the bond of the covenant is the new covenant in Hebrews: “For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord”. After those days means after we are delivered out of here, out of this new Egypt, America.

“I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people”. Meaning we are going to know God's laws and we will keep God's laws. Right now it can be routine: you go to work every day, stop in the donut store for a donut and your coffee, eat the donut, and then remember, damn, it's the days of unleavened bread, how could I forget? But the Lord God says his laws will be in our minds. We are not going to forget, and we will do them and serve him. That is the new covenant. We are in the beginning of it now, but once Christ returns it will be fully established in the wilderness.

“And they shall not teach every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest.” All of us will know the Lord, from the least amongst us to the greatest. You won't have to go and teach anybody, because the Lord is going to teach us. Every custom and thought we learned in America has to go, and he will show us even the parts we are missing now, like the sun and the moon working together for the times and seasons, wisdom destroyed from amongst us through slavery.

So being brought into the bond of the covenant is us being purged in the wilderness again. As he pleaded with our fathers and got rid of the leaven from amongst them, he will “purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me”: those that break God's laws, those with leaven in them. Many will be delivered out of here, but not everyone is going to make it into the promised land. Those who enter will have his laws written in their hearts.

precepts.text: In the holy mountain, at the return, all Israel shall serve the Most High, and there He will require the offerings again.
precepts.point: In our captivity, with no Levitical priesthood and no temple, keeping the commandments is the offering and the reasonable service: he that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough, and we present our bodies a living sacrifice, sacrificing the lusts and pleasures of the flesh to follow the footsteps of Christ. And Ezekiel 20 shows that when Israel is brought back through the wilderness, offerings will be required again in the holy mountain.

note.label: Leviticus 1: The Law of the Burnt Offerings

precepts.why:
The offerings are not gone forever. Ezekiel shows that when Israel is brought back through the wilderness, they will be required again: “For in mine holy mountain, in the mountain of the height of Israel, saith the Lord God, there shall all the house of Israel, all of them in the land, serve me: there will I accept them, and there will I require your offerings, and the firstfruits of your oblations, with all your holy things.”

In the holy mountain, at the return, all the house of Israel shall serve the Most High, and there He will require the offerings again. So the law of the burnt offering is not a dead letter; in captivity our offering is keeping the commandments and presenting our bodies a living sacrifice, and in the land the offerings return.

precepts.text: What comes into the mind to be as the heathen serving wood and stone shall not be, for the Most High rules with a mighty hand and fury poured out until his people acknowledge him.
precepts.point: The Most High sends to them by his messengers, rising up early and sending because he had compassion, but they mock the messengers, despise his words, and misuse his prophets until the wrath of the Lord arises and there is no remedy.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 36: The Captivity of Judah into Babylon

precepts.why:
Israel said in their mind, “We will be as the heathen, as the families of the countries, to serve wood and stone.” The Most High answers, “that which cometh into your mind shall not be at all.”

That is what the chief of the priests and the people did in Zedekiah’s days: they “transgressed very much after all the abominations of the heathen.” They wanted to be like the nations. But he will not let his people become the heathen: “As I live, saith the Lord God, surely with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out, will I rule over you.”

So the wrath that arose against his people, till there was no remedy, is that fury poured out. The Most High rules over Israel with a mighty hand until his people acknowledge him.

precepts.text: The large place ties to being brought into the wilderness of the people, where the Most High delivers again.
precepts.point: They prevented him in the day of his calamity, but the Lord was his stay and brought him forth into a large place because he delighted in him.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“He brought me forth also into a large place; he delivered me, because he delighted in me.” That large place ties to Ezekiel: “And I will bring you into the wilderness of the people, and there will I plead with you face to face.”

The Most High brings us into the wilderness of the people and pleads with us face to face there. That is where he delivers again, bringing us out into a large place because he delights in us, the way he was David's stay in the day of his calamity.

precepts.text: A land flowing with milk and honey, the glory of all lands, which is Jerusalem, our homeland; so laying in green pastures is going into peace.
precepts.point: The green pastures are peace and the beauty of the land: the grass, the cattle, the flowers of the field. It is going into the homeland, the glory of all lands, which is Jerusalem, Israel.

note.label: Psalm 23: The Lord Is My Shepherd

precepts.why:
“He maketh me to lie down in green pastures”. What are these green pastures? Ezekiel tells of the land the Most High espied for us when he brought us out of Egypt: “In the day that I lifted up mine hand unto them, to bring them forth of the land of Egypt into a land that I had espied for them, flowing with milk and honey, which is the glory of all lands”.

A land flowing with milk and honey, the glory of all lands, which is Jerusalem, our homeland. The green pastures are peace and the beauty of the land: the grass, the cattle, the flowers of the field. So lying down in green pastures is going into peace, going into the homeland, Jerusalem, Israel.

precepts.text: You shall not do after the doings of the land of Egypt or of Canaan, which is why the idols of Egypt point to the immoral laws that follow in that chapter.
precepts.point: They rebelled and would not cast away the abominations of their eyes nor forsake the idols of Egypt, so He said He would pour out His fury, but He wrought for His name's sake that it should not be polluted before the heathen.

note.label: Ezekiel 20: I Will Not Be Inquired Of

precepts.why:
When He brought them out of Egypt the Most High said, “Cast ye away every man the abominations of his eyes, and defile not yourselves with the idols of Egypt”. What are the idols of Egypt? Leviticus 18 tells you: “After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do: and after the doings of the land of Canaan, whither I bring you, shall ye not do: neither shall ye walk in their ordinances.”

The doings of Egypt are the immoral laws laid out in the rest of that chapter. The idols of Egypt and the doings of Egypt point to the same thing: the abominations of their eyes that they were commanded to cast away.

They rebelled and “would not hearken”; they did not cast away the abominations of their eyes, “neither did they forsake the idols of Egypt”. So He said He would pour out His fury upon them in the midst of Egypt, but He “wrought for my name’s sake, that it should not be polluted before the heathen”. And the doings of spiritual Egypt today still apply: they are not to be done.

precepts.text: Because they changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into images, He gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, which is what being given statutes that are not good goes into.
precepts.point: Because they refused His law He gave them also statutes that were not good and judgments whereby they should not live, giving His own people over to their own ways and to passing their children through the fire.

note.label: Ezekiel 20: I Will Not Be Inquired Of

precepts.why:
“Wherefore I gave them also statutes that were not good, and judgments whereby they should not live”. Paul goes into what that is. They “changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.” Their eyes were after their fathers' idols. “Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves”.

That is being given statutes that are not good. Because they refused His law, walked not in His statutes and polluted His sabbaths, He gave His own people over to their own ways, even to passing their children through the fire, “that I might make them desolate”. They “changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator”.

This is also why we are scattered across the four corners of the globe today: He lifted up His hand in the wilderness to scatter them among the heathen because they despised His statutes and polluted His sabbaths, and it is the same thing today.

precepts.text: Those delivered from the noise of the archers shall rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord, meaning we practice now how we will play when it is game time in the wilderness.
precepts.point: The way you rehearse and practice now is how you will play in the wilderness, and Christ can read minds, so those who are fronting, faking, and holding secret hate may be purged out and called rebels.

note.label: Ezekiel 20: I Will Not Be Inquired Of

precepts.why:
“They that are delivered from the noise of archers in the places of drawing water, there shall they rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord”. Rehearse. The way you rehearse and practice now is how you will play when it is game time in the wilderness.

The Most High will bring us out from the people, gather us out of the countries, separate us from the heathen we wanted to be like, and bring us “into the wilderness of the people”, where He will “plead with you face to face” and teach us everything we do not yet know of this Bible. Pleaded means what it meant for our fathers: “Like as I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so will I plead with you”. He put them to death there, and it will be the same when we go back to the wilderness. With a mighty hand, a stretched out arm and fury poured out He will rule, which means two-thirds of us must go for the Most High to rule, and that is prophesied.

He causes us to pass under the rod and brings us into the bond of the covenant, and He will “purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me”. Christ can read minds. Those who are fronting, faking and holding secret hate may be purged out and called rebels, and “they shall not enter into the land of Israel”. So rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord now.

precepts.point: When Paul says he conferred not with flesh and blood, he means no man taught him the doctrine or the gospel; Christ revealed it directly.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
Ezekiel confirms that Israel in sin is called the heathen. The Lord says to “the house of Israel”, “Are ye polluted after the manner of your fathers? and commit ye whoredom after their abominations?” They made their sons pass through the fire and polluted themselves with idols, and “that which cometh into your mind shall not be at all, that ye say, We will be as the heathen, as the families of the countries, to serve wood and stone.”

When Israel is in sin they are saying “We will be as the heathen.” That is who Paul was sent to preach Christ among: the Israelites who were following the customs of other nations. And when he says he “conferred not with flesh and blood”, he means no man taught him the doctrine or the gospel; Christ revealed it directly.

precepts.point: They are called brethren of the Gentiles. Romans 9:3-4 proves the apostles' brethren are Israelites.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Verse 9 introduces a third term: the heathen. Paul was sent to the heathen, the same people called uncircumcision and Gentiles. Ezekiel shows who they are. God rebukes Israel for idolatry: “when ye make your sons to pass through the fire, ye pollute yourselves with all your idols, even unto this day: and shall I be enquired of by you, O house of Israel? As I live, saith the Lord God, I will not be enquired of by you.”

Then: “And that which cometh into your mind shall not be at all, that ye say, We will be as the heathen, as the families of the countries, to serve wood and stone.” Israel declared “We will be as the heathen” by following other nations' customs. When Israelites go outside their laws and follow other nations, they are called heathens.

note.label: America Is A Reflection Of Ancient Assyria | PART 2

precepts.why: We’re going to be caught up, and then what? A Christian said we’re just going to stay in the air; you got to read precept upon precept. “I will bring you into the wilderness of the people”: the same wilderness we were in during the time of Moses. “Like as I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt”: that’s the proof. “I will bring you into the bond of the covenant”: he’s going to teach us the law all over again. “I will purge out from among you the rebels”: certain men and women who were sneakily evil on this side; brothers and sisters didn’t catch their BS, but the Lord sees it. He will bring them into the wilderness just to kill them, because if you’re rebellious here you’re going to be rebellious there. “They shall not enter into the land of Israel.”

“And that which cometh into your mind shall not be at all, that ye say, We will be as the heathen.” Our people always want to be like the white man, like the other nations; we want to be everybody but who we are, the children of Israel.

“As the families of the countries, to serve wood and stone”: we want to worship idols just like everybody else. That is the mentality of Christians and Muslims.

Face to face: Paul told us about this. “For now we see through a glass, darkly”: right now we see through a glass darkly; we don’t never claim to know everything. “But then face to face”: then, in the wilderness, face to face.

“Now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.” In the wilderness he’s going to reveal who we are. That part right there is a heavy meaning; we never really touch on that too much, but it’s heavy. Say you’ve got Deacon Malachi here: that’s how we know him. On that day, when we are speaking with the Lord face to face, he’s going to reveal who everybody is from the beginning, what your real name is. You might think your name is Shaniqua or Ray Ray; he’s going to give you your true name, and we’re all going to see from the beginning. God knows us from the beginning, and we’re going to know from that far back.

Paul said the same thing about the wilderness: “Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea; And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea”.

“Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.” He’s talking about back then, when we were in the wilderness, and he says that’s an example to us. When you read the chapter, he goes step by step through things that occurred in the wilderness with Moses.

Paul sums it up: “Now all these things happened unto them for ensamples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come”. Because then we are at the end of the world: what happened to our fathers in the wilderness of Egypt is written for us, who will be brought into the wilderness of the people.

Here’s the bond of the covenant. Right now many of us speak reckless; watch this. “In that day there shall be a fountain opened to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem for sin and for uncleanness.”

“I will cut off the names of the idols out of the land, and they shall no more be remembered”: ain’t none of the idols that’s here going to be remembered no more. “And also I will cause the prophets and the unclean spirit to pass out of the land”: that’s these reverends, the popes, these fake ministers, the imams. They’re all going to be passed out of the land through destruction.

“When any shall yet prophesy, then his father and his mother that begat him shall say unto him, Thou shalt not live; for thou speakest lies in the name of the Lord: and his father and his mother that begat him shall thrust him through when he prophesieth.” Here’s the bond of the covenant. You have brothers and sisters right now that talk reckless, but watch on this day. That’s the bond: ain’t no more ‘oh I’m sorry, can I repent.’ No.

Christ said the same thing. The Lord ain’t going to play with nobody. Right now everybody is talking, you talk your little smack, you sit home and you murmur; you wait to that day. “But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.” That’s what the Son of God says, and that’s about the wilderness.

In the wilderness we’re not in the kingdom yet. It’s going to be the same as with our forefathers when they came up out of Egypt: the temptations, the disobedience, the murmurings, and Christ purging out the rebels. “But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me”: this is before we enter into the kingdom; it’s the wilderness where the trial starts, like 1 Corinthians 10, where our forefathers murmured, fell to fornication and were destroyed of the destroyer. Remember Shaka Zulu, Dracula Untold, Ivan the Terrible, with everybody hanging on spears; that’s what Christ is going to do under the bond of the strictness of the covenant, when grace and mercy is over.

There are different stages to the New Covenant; I hope you novices took notes. “For the Lord shall be thine everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall be ended”: is this happening in the wilderness or in the kingdom? In the kingdom. “Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever”: when we’re in the kingdom. “A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation”.

The bond and strictness of the covenant is us in the wilderness; when we enter into the kingdom the Most High is going to put his laws in our mind and heart, we’ll be all righteous, and there’ll be no need to preach to your neighbour how to keep the commandments. It’s not going to be like now, where you just be like, ah, let me listen to what he’s talking about on Friday. You’re going to get your ass whooped in the wilderness, bad.

note.label: Do You Know What Happened To Rasheem Carter?

points: “And I will cause you to pass under the rod”, “I will bring you into the bond of the covenant”: meaning you’re going to get corrected or rejected once your wickedness is detected.

note.label: Do You Know What Happened To Rasheem Carter?

points: “And I will purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me”. Some of you are still going to be trying to challenge Christ and the prophets; the only difference is we’re going to have big boots. You’re going to get a foot in that ass; it’s going to be so spectacular, because we can’t get you now, but then we’re going to get you. “I will bring them forth out of the country where they sojourn, and they shall not enter into the land of Israel: and ye shall know that I am the Lord.” Negroes will be gone in that day; it’s going to be glorious.

Some of you are going to get delivered only to be destroyed, because he needs some crash test dummies, so y’all be like, yo, don’t play with this man. Tyrone was running his mouth and all of a sudden his lips hit the floor; we didn’t even see when Christ put the sword back in. If Peter could chop off a centurion’s ear, you don’t think he could chop up somebody’s lips? So some of you Negroes exist only to get judgment later on. That’s why I don’t mind the Negroes: let them talk. You wicked Israelites in other groups, you stay there; you don’t know this Bible, you don’t know what you’re being lined up for. If you was hating men now teaching the word, you think you’re going to come in the wilderness and get a pass?

note.label: Do You Know What Happened To Rasheem Carter?

points: This is what takes place once we get caught up in the air. “And I will bring you out from the people”: we are going to be brought out from amongst the people we were living among. When that war takes place and them bombs drop, the angels are going to deliver us, we are going to be changed in the twinkling of an eye, and we are going to be brought up from amongst the people.

“And will gather you out of the countries wherein ye are scattered, with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out”: he is going to be doing a lot of killing while he is delivering us. He is telling the angels to deliver us while he is killing people and destroying armies.

“And I will bring you into the wilderness of the people”: after World War III, after Christ destroys the armies of the earth, the Israelites, you so-called Negroes, Puerto Ricans, North American Indians, you children of the slave trade, will be taken into the wilderness, the same way we were in the wilderness with Moses. That is why Paul keeps warning us in Corinthians not to murmur like our forefathers in the wilderness and not to be adulterers like our forefathers in the wilderness: Paul understood that we are going back into the wilderness again.

“And there will I plead with you face to face”: Christ is going to teach us face to face. He is going to say, this is what this means; that new moon you see bright in the sky, that’s a new moon. Some people are going to make it up out of here, but they are not going to get the kingdom.

“Like as I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so will I plead with you, saith the Lord God”: the same way the Lord pleaded with us when he brought us out of Egypt, he will plead with us again.

“And I will cause you to pass under the rod”: the rod is correction. Christ is going to teach us the laws, and nobody better say nada. Where Christ says, ‘these my enemies that don’t want me to rule over them, bring them hither and slay them before me’, that is talking about the wilderness. Say Christ returns and tells a deacon, you are over everybody here, you are one of the twelve, and gives him an order. And you say, I want to talk to Christ, I don’t want to hear what he says; I know this dude from back in Babylon, I never really liked this dude. They won’t necessarily be coming against Christ: it is the men that Christ set up that they are going to be fighting against in the wilderness. The same thing will happen again; they will be murmuring, and some people are going to be delivered up out of here just to be made an example of.

“And I will bring you into the bond of the covenant”: the new covenant. We are under the new covenant right now; that is why we are able to repent, and why we are not put to death if we commit adultery. But Christ is going to bring us under the bond of the new covenant.

“And I will purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me”: there are going to be people in the wilderness that are rebellious, that murmur, that still want to fornicate, that speak evil and hate dignities. The Lord is going to purge them out from amongst us, and this happens in the wilderness.

“I will bring them forth out of the country where they sojourn”: Christ will bring you out from there, the chariots are going to come and deliver you, and you’ll be like, I made it, damn, I did some evil stuff the day before yesterday, how come I made it? And you are going to be brought into the wilderness.

“And they shall not enter into the land of Israel”: you are not going to enter into the kingdom. So brothers and sisters, making it up out of Babylon is not the end of it. Those that transgress the law are going to die.

There are going to be different levels. The 144 is going to be on another level, and the 12 on another level. Them that transgress is not talking about the 144 or the 12; it is talking about that mixed multitude that no man could number. The scripture says the 144 are going to be like the gods on the earth; other people will live forever, but the 144 and the 12 are on another level.
